full_text_en:
Orient International Group Shanghai Foreign Trade Co., Ltd. v. Lanzhou Jincheng Tourism Service (Group) Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Confirmation of Guarantee Contract Relationship (Appeal)

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Orient International Group Shanghai Foreign Trade Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Liu Jianwei, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Chen Xu, an employee of the company.

Agent ad litem: Guo Feng, lawyer of Beijing Dingming Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Lanzhou Jincheng Tourism Service (Group) Co., Ltd.

Legal Representative: Wang Xuguo, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Ran Zhijiang, lawyer of Beijing Gongcheng Law Firm.

The Appellant, Orient International Group Shanghai Foreign Trade Co., Ltd. (formerly Shanghai Foreign Trade Corporation, hereinafter referred to as "Shanghai Foreign Trade"), appealed to the Supreme People's Court against the civil judgment on guarantee contract relationship rendered by the Gansu High People's Court in the case of dispute over confirmation of guarantee contract relationship with the Respondent, Lanzhou Jincheng Tourism Service (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Jincheng Company").

The Supreme People's Court found upon trial:

On February 27, 1995, Shanghai Foreign Trade and Tian Fengnian, the legal representative of a third party, Hungarian Jincheng Haoke International Trade Liability Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Haoke Company"), signed a sales contract numbered 95HTI4E025, stipulating that Shanghai Foreign Trade would supply Haoke Company with children's acrylic-cotton padded jackets and children's down jackets of different specifications, totaling 28,000 PCS (i.e., 28,000 pieces), with a total amount of USD 365,600, allowing a 5% increase or decrease in shipment quantity; the price term was CIF Budapest; the shipment period was from July to August 1995; the port of shipment was Shanghai, China; the destination was Budapest, Hungary; the payment term was telegraphic transfer within 70 days after the bill of lading date; quality objections were to be raised by the buyer within 30 days from the date of arrival of the goods at the port of destination; quantity objections were to be raised by the buyer within 15 days from the date of arrival of the goods at the port of destination; claims were to be supported by inspection certificates from an independent surveyor acceptable to the seller. Zheng Yi, a business representative of Shanghai Foreign Trade, and Tian Fengnian, the legal representative of Haoke Company, signed the contract. On April 20 of the same year, Jincheng Company issued to Shanghai Foreign Trade a letter of guarantee for "Hungarian Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company." The letter stated: "Hungarian Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company is an overseas enterprise dispatched by Lanzhou Jincheng Tourism Service (Group) Co., Ltd. Regarding the import and export contracts signed between your company and this company this year, we agree to act as the economic guarantor for the contracts. We hope for smooth cooperation." After the sales contract was signed, Shanghai Foreign Trade faxed the container shipment status to Haoke Company on July 20, 1995, and loaded the goods onto a vessel on July 26 of the same year, obtained the bill of lading and delivered it to Haoke Company. Subsequently, because a portion of the goods under the contract was confiscated by Hungarian customs and another portion went missing, Haoke Company did not pay the货款 to Shanghai Foreign Trade, leading to a dispute. Shanghai Foreign Trade then applied for arbitration to the Shanghai Sub-Commission of the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission (hereinafter referred to as the "Shanghai Arbitration Sub-Commission") on March 8, 1996, requesting that Haoke Company immediately pay Shanghai Foreign Trade USD 328,478 in货款, compensate for losses, and bear the arbitration costs. The Shanghai Arbitration Sub-Commission held that Shanghai Foreign Trade had fulfilled its obligations under the sales contract by loading the goods, paying the freight to the destination Budapest, promptly notifying Haoke Company after loading, bearing all costs and risks before the goods were loaded onto the vessel, and providing a full set of shipping documents. However, Haoke Company, after receiving the full set of original shipping documents, failed to pay the purchase price as stipulated in the contract, which constituted a fundamental breach of contract and should bear liability for breach, compensating Shanghai Foreign Trade for the economic losses caused by Haoke Company's breach. The Shanghai Arbitration Sub-Commission then rendered an award (97) Hu Mao Zhong Zi No. 505 on August 29, 1997, ordering Haoke Company to pay Shanghai Foreign Trade USD 328,478 in货款; Haoke Company to compensate Shanghai Foreign Trade for economic losses of USD 21,040; 90% of the arbitration fees to be borne by Haoke Company and 10% by Shanghai Foreign Trade; and Haoke Company to reimburse Shanghai Foreign Trade for legal representation fees of RMB 186,000. Because the said arbitration award did not address the guarantee liability of Jincheng Company, Shanghai Foreign Trade filed a lawsuit with the Gansu High People's Court on February 19, 1998, seeking a judgment ordering Jincheng Company to assume guarantee liability of USD 383,883.88 and compensate for interest losses. During the litigation, Shanghai Foreign Trade filed an application with the original trial court on March 24 of the same year, stating that in the case of Shanghai Foreign Trade v. Jincheng Company for guarantee liability compensation, since the amount of compensation was subject to the result of enforcement against Haoke Company, the claim in this case was changed to seek a judicial confirmation that the guarantee contract of Jincheng Company was valid and that Jincheng Company should bear guarantee compensation liability.

It was also found: On March 16, 1995, Jincheng Company issued a letter of guarantee to a third party, Shanghai Knitwear Import and Export Company, with the same content as the guarantee letter it issued to Shanghai Foreign Trade on April 20 of the same year. Regarding the issuance of the guarantee letter by Jincheng Company, the company admitted that the guarantee letter to Shanghai Knitwear Import and Export Company was issued by it. As to whether the company had issued a guarantee letter with the same content to Shanghai Foreign Trade, the original trial judgment found that the guarantee letter to Shanghai Foreign Trade was issued by the company, and Jincheng Company did not appeal this finding; during the second instance of the Supreme People's Court, Jincheng Company stated that it had not issued a guarantee letter to Shanghai Foreign Trade, and could not confirm whether the official seal of Jincheng Company affixed on the guarantee letter was genuine, but Jincheng Company did not apply for an appraisal of this seal. Regarding the name of Haoke Company, the original trial court had commissioned the Department of Foreign Languages of Lanzhou University to translate the name of Haoke Company, confirming it as "Jincheng Enterprise Group Haoke Company." When Jincheng Company issued the guarantee letters to Shanghai Foreign Trade and to the third party Shanghai Knitwear Import and Export Company, it referred to Haoke Company as "Hungarian Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company." When Shanghai Foreign Trade applied for arbitration to the Shanghai Arbitration Sub-Commission, it referred to the respondent Haoke Company as "Hungarian Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company," and Haoke Company also submitted written defense in the name of "Hungarian Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company." In a letter dated June 20, 1996, to Shanghai Foreign Trade regarding the selection of the presiding arbitrator, Haoke Company signed off as "Hungarian Jincheng Haoke Company" and affixed its official seal. In a report dated March 28, 1996, from Haoke Company to Jincheng Company, it stated that the sales contract in question was signed between Shanghai Foreign Trade and "Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company." In a reply letter dated April 8, 1998, from the Secretariat of the Shanghai Arbitration Sub-Commission to Shanghai Foreign Trade, it confirmed that Shanghai Foreign Trade had applied for arbitration against "Hungarian Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company" as the respondent, and the respondent had initially defended in the name of "Hungarian Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company," but subsequently appeared in arbitration documents under the names "Jincheng Haoke International Trade Liability Co., Ltd.," "Jincheng Haoke International Trade Co., Ltd.," and "Hungarian Jincheng Haoke Company" (with identical company seals). Due to the inconsistency in the respondent's names, the arbitral tribunal had requested it to confirm its own name. On November 27, 1996, the respondent wrote to the Shanghai Arbitration Sub-Commission stating, "The full name of the company is Jincheng Haoke International Trade Liability Co., Ltd." The Shanghai Arbitration Sub-Commission held that "the above facts indicate that although the respondent used the various names mentioned, it was still the same entity." During the first and second instances of the litigation, Jincheng Company did not provide evidence to prove that it had a second Haoke Company in Hungary.

The original trial court held after trial: The guaranteed party listed in the guarantee letter of Jincheng Company was "Hungarian Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company," which was not the same company as the guaranteed party sued by Shanghai Foreign Trade or the respondent listed in the arbitration award, nor was it the same as the buyer under the main contract. It could not be confirmed that there was a legal relationship of creditor and guarantor between Shanghai Foreign Trade and Jincheng Company. The reasons for the lawsuit by Shanghai Foreign Trade lacked factual and legal basis. In accordance with Article 54 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, the court ruled: The claims of Shanghai Foreign Trade were dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 31,200 was to be borne by Shanghai Foreign Trade.

Shanghai Foreign Trade appealed against the aforementioned civil judgment of the original trial court, with the following grounds: The finding of the original trial court that "the guaranteed party listed in the guarantee letter was Hungarian Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company, which was not the same company as the guaranteed party sued by the plaintiff or the respondent in the arbitration, nor was it the same as the buyer under the main contract" was inconsistent with the facts. The actual situation was that the guaranteed party, as a Hungarian company, although using multiple names expressed in different scripts, could not change its nature as the same entity in the legal relationship. There was ample evidence to prove this fact during the execution of the main contract with Shanghai Foreign Trade and in the arbitration process. Although the guaranteed party used different names, they all had the same business premises, same telephone number, used the same Hungarian official seal, and performed the rights and obligations under the same contract through the same general manager, Tian Fengnian. The original trial court's rash determination that the entities were different solely based on different textual expressions of names was erroneous. There existed a legal relationship of creditor and guarantor between Shanghai Foreign Trade and Jincheng Company. From the date Jincheng Company issued the guarantee letter to Shanghai Foreign Trade on April 20, 1995, a guarantee contract relationship was established between the two parties. The original judgment had unclear findings of fact and improper application of law, so the appellant requested the reversal of the original judgment, amended judgment ordering Jincheng Company to assume compensation liability for the debts of Haoke Company, and to bear the litigation costs.

Jincheng Company responded: The key witnesses to prove the authenticity and establishment of the guarantee letter dated April 20, 1995, submitted by Shanghai Foreign Trade were the three handling persons Jin Ting, Zheng Yi, and Tian Fengnian. Jin Ting and Zheng Yi were business representatives of Shanghai Foreign Trade, and they did not appear in court to testify or provide testimony. Tian Fengnian was not only a necessary witness but also the judgment debtor in the enforcement of the foreign-related arbitration award applied for by Shanghai Foreign Trade. Shanghai Foreign Trade neither listed the guaranteed party as a co-defendant nor provided sufficient evidence, merely relying on a piece of paper to demand that Jincheng Company assume responsibility for an unascertained guaranteed party, and to demand that Jincheng Company bear compensation liability for a main contract that had no guarantee clause and excluded third-party liability. Such claims should not be supported. Jincheng Company did not participate in the arbitration hearing between Shanghai Foreign Trade and Haoke Company, and thus could not cross-examine or defend the facts of that case. Jincheng Company had no such litigation rights, nor was it obligated to confirm facts or assume compensation liability on behalf of the applicant or respondent in the arbitration case. Therefore, Jincheng Company requested the second instance court to dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The Supreme People's Court held: This case involves two different legal relationships: one between Shanghai Foreign Trade and Haoke Company, and another between Shanghai Foreign Trade and Jincheng Company. Regarding the dispute over the international goods sales contract between Shanghai Foreign Trade and Haoke Company, the Shanghai Arbitration Sub-Commission has already rendered an award (97) Hu Mao Zhong Zi No. 505, ordering Haoke Company to assume civil liability for payment of货款 and compensation for losses to Shanghai Foreign Trade, meaning the scope of the principal obligor's debt has been determined. Since the award of the Shanghai Arbitration Sub-Commission cannot involve parties outside the arbitration agreement, i.e., the guarantor Jincheng Company in the accessory contract, Shanghai Foreign Trade is entitled to file a separate lawsuit against Jincheng Company as the defendant in the original trial court solely regarding the guarantee contract relationship in this case, seeking confirmation of the existence of a guarantee contract relationship between Shanghai Foreign Trade and Jincheng Company and an order for Jincheng Company to assume compensation liability for the debts of the principal obligor, Haoke Company. The original trial judgment has already found that the guarantee letter dated April 20, 1995, was issued by Jincheng Company. Jincheng Company did not appeal this finding and did not raise any objection to the facts found by the original trial. During the second instance of this court, although Jincheng Company stated that it had not issued the guarantee letter, it could not give a definite answer as to whether the official seal affixed on the guarantee letter was genuine, and it did not apply for an appraisal of this seal. Therefore, it should be determined that the guarantee letter was issued by Jincheng Company. Regarding the name of the guaranteed party Haoke Company, although Haoke Company had multiple Chinese names, it used the same seal, and its legal representative was the same person, Tian Fengnian. Moreover, Jincheng Company could not prove that it had established a second Haoke Company in Hungary. Therefore, it should be determined that the guaranteed party referred to as "Hungarian Jincheng Enterprise Group Europe Haoke Company" in the guarantee letter was the same as the principal obligor Haoke Company under the main contract. A guarantee contract relationship had been formed between Shanghai Foreign Trade and Jincheng Company. This contract reflected the true intent of the parties and was not illegal, so it should be held valid. Accordingly, all the defenses of Jincheng Company lacked factual and legal basis, and its arguments were not accepted. The original trial judgment had unclear findings of fact and improper application of law, which should be corrected. The grounds of appeal of Shanghai Foreign Trade were established and should be supported. Given that the guarantee letter involved in this case did not specify what type of guarantee liability the guarantor should assume, and that the act of guarantee occurred before the implementation of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, in accordance with Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning Guarantees in Economic Contract Disputes, which states "if the guarantee contract does not stipulate what type of guarantee liability the guarantor should assume, or the stipulation is unclear, the guarantor shall be deemed to assume compensation liability," Jincheng Company should assume compensation liability for the debts of the guaranteed party Haoke Company for payment of货款 and compensation for losses. Accordingly, in accordance with Items (2) and (3) of Paragraph 1 of Article 153 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Supreme People's Court rendered the following judgment on April 24, 1999:

1. The civil judgment (1998) Gan Jing Chu Zi No. 17 of the Gansu High People's Court is reversed.

2. It is confirmed that the guarantee letter issued by Lanzhou Jincheng Tourism Service (Group) Co., Ltd. to Orient International Group Shanghai Foreign Trade Co., Ltd. is established, and a guarantee contract relationship has been formed between the two parties.

3. Lanzhou Jincheng Tourism Service (Group) Co., Ltd. shall assume compensation liability for the debts of Hungarian Jincheng Haoke International Trade Liability Co., Ltd. to pay货款 and compensate for losses to Orient International Group Shanghai Foreign Trade Co., Ltd., as determined by the award (97) Hu Mao Zhong Zi No. 505 of the Shanghai Sub-Commission of the China International Economic and Trade Arbitration Commission.

The case acceptance fees for the first and second instances, each RMB 31,200, totaling RMB 62,400, shall be borne by Lanzhou Jincheng Tourism Service (Group) Co., Ltd.
